summary: Choline fenofibrate (brand Trilipix) is the choline salt of fenofibric acid, a fibrate and PPAR-alpha agonist used as an adjunct to diet to lower triglycerides in severe hypertriglyceridemia and to improve the overall lipid profile in mixed dyslipidemia. Unlike fenofibrate, it delivers fenofibric acid directly and was available as delayed-release capsules. In the United States the brand Trilipix has been discontinued and the drug is no longer available as a standalone product; fibrate effects on cardiovascular morbidity and mortality have not been established.
indications: Adjunct to diet for treatment of adults with severe hypertriglyceridemia
Adjunct to diet to reduce triglycerides and increase HDL-cholesterol, and to reduce LDL-cholesterol, total cholesterol, and apolipoprotein B in adults with mixed dyslipidemia

moa: Choline fenofibrate dissociates to fenofibric acid, the active moiety, which activates peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPAR-alpha). Activation increases lipolysis and elimination of triglyceride-rich particles by inducing lipoprotein lipase and reducing apoprotein C-III. The resulting fall in triglycerides shifts LDL toward larger, more buoyant particles, while PPAR-alpha stimulation increases synthesis of apolipoproteins A-I and A-II and raises HDL-cholesterol. Fenofibric acid also lowers serum uric acid.

absolute: Severe renal impairment, including patients on dialysis
Active liver disease, including primary biliary cirrhosis and unexplained persistent liver function abnormalities
Known hypersensitivity to choline fenofibrate, fenofibrate, or fenofibric acid
relative: Concomitant statin therapy (increased risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis)
Concomitant oral anticoagulants (potentiation of anticoagulant effect)
Mild to moderate renal impairment (dose reduction required)
monitor: Creatine kinase if muscle symptoms occur

preg: Human data are limited. Animal studies showed adverse developmental effects at maternally toxic doses. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Use during breastfeeding is not recommended because of the potential for serious adverse reactions and tumorigenicity observed in animal studies. A decision should be made to discontinue nursing or discontinue the drug.
renal: Choline fenofibrate is contraindicated in severe renal impairment, including dialysis patients. In mild to moderate renal impairment, initiate at 45 mg once daily and increase only after evaluating effects on renal function and lipid levels. Monitor renal function, particularly in the elderly, as fenofibric acid exposure rises with reduced clearance; reversible elevations in serum creatinine have been reported.
hepatic: Choline fenofibrate is contraindicated in active liver disease, including primary biliary cirrhosis and unexplained persistent liver function abnormalities. It can increase serum transaminases; monitor liver enzymes periodically and discontinue if levels persist above three times the upper limit of normal.

major: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (statins) - increased risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis
Oral anticoagulants (warfarin) - potentiation of anticoagulant effect, monitor INR closely
moderate: Cyclosporine and other nephrotoxic immunosuppressants (increased risk of renal dysfunction)
Bile acid sequestrants (may bind fenofibric acid; separate dosing by at least 1 hour before or 4-6 hours after)
minor: Highly protein-bound drugs may be displaced
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food (delayed-release formulation); maintain a lipid-lowering diet
interactions.alcohol: Excess alcohol can worsen hypertriglyceridemia and hepatic risk; limit alcohol intake
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate serum transaminases and creatinine and lower serum uric acid, which can affect interpretation of liver, renal, and lipid testing

serious: Venous thromboembolism (pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis)
rare: Severe hypersensitivity and cutaneous reactions (Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis)
emergency: Rhabdomyolysis (severe muscle pain, weakness, dark urine) - stop drug and seek emergency care
Acute pancreatitis (severe abdominal pain radiating to the back) - emergency care
Severe allergic skin reaction with blistering - emergency care

monitoring: Fasting lipid panel at baseline and periodically
Liver function tests at baseline and periodically; discontinue if persistently above 3x ULN
Serum creatinine and renal function, especially in the elderly and those on cyclosporine
Creatine kinase if muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness occurs
Complete blood count periodically during early therapy
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed and continue your low-fat diet, exercise, and weight management
Swallow the capsule whole; do not open, crush, or chew it
Report muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness, especially with fever or dark urine
Report yellowing of the skin or eyes, severe stomach pain, or right-upper abdominal pain
Tell your doctor about all medicines, especially statins and blood thinners, and limit alcohol
pk: Lipid effects develop over weeks; assess response after about 2 months
Tmax approximately 4-5 hours for fenofibric acid (delayed-release)
Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C; protect from moisture
pearls: Choline fenofibrate is the choline salt of fenofibric acid, the active PPAR-alpha agonist moiety, delivered as a delayed-release capsule that can be taken with or without food
Used as an adjunct to diet for severe hypertriglyceridemia and mixed dyslipidemia; typical dose was 135 mg once daily with a 45 mg lower strength available
In the United States the brand Trilipix has been discontinued and the drug is no longer marketed as a standalone product; prescribing data derive from prior FDA labeling, EMA, and BNF sources
As a fibrate, carries risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis (heightened with statins), cholelithiasis, hepatotoxicity, reversible serum creatinine elevation, and pancreatitis
Contraindicated in severe renal impairment, active liver disease, and gallbladder disease; fibrates have not been shown to reduce cardiovascular morbidity or mortality
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular once-daily schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: There is no specific antidote. Management is supportive with general symptomatic measures; because fenofibric acid is highly protein bound, it is not appreciably removed by hemodialysis. Contact Poison Control (1-800-222-1222).
